headline: Google Assistant to shut down Sept 2026, Gemini becomes default AI across Android, Apple, cars
summary: Google Assistant will be phased out from mobile devices, Wear OS, and headphones starting September 4, 2026, with Gemini taking its place across a vast ecosystem, including Apple's Siri.
details: Google is phasing out its voice assistant, Google Assistant, starting September 4, 2026. This shutdown will affect mobile devices, Wear OS watches, and compatible headphones, with Gemini becoming the mandatory replacement. The standalone Gemini app already surpassed one billion monthly active users in August 2026.

The strategy emphasizes distribution, with Gemini integrated into core Android functions. Corner swipes and long presses that previously summoned Assistant now activate Gemini. Samsung's One UI builds increasingly incorporate Gemini extensions into productivity apps, even assigning it to the side button by default.

Gemini's reach extends beyond Android. In January 2026, Apple confirmed that its next Foundation Models for Siri would be based on Gemini, making Siri downstream of Google's AI. This marks a significant cross-platform integration for Google.

The automotive sector is also seeing a major shift. General Motors pushed an OTA update in April-May 2026, swapping Google Assistant for Gemini in roughly four million vehicles. Volvo is following suit, shipping Gemini in its new EX60 electric SUV for real-time parking sign and road marking analysis.

Beyond embedded car systems, Android Auto, with over 250 million compatible vehicles, is undergoing a separate Gemini rollout. This positions Gemini as the default AI for hardware makers who opt not to develop their own models.

Google TV also received natural language system controls for Gemini in June 2026, debuting on select TCL sets before expanding to other brands. Further integrations include Insta360's GO Ultra camera, which added a Gemini-backed assistant named Kira for live translation and visual questions in August 2026.

Smart eyewear is another frontier, with XREAL's upcoming Project Aura pairing Android XR with Gemini in a glasses form factor. Google's comprehensive offering, from wake word to visual recognition, allows manufacturers to integrate Gemini at various depths.

The article suggests that only a court order could plausibly disrupt this compounding distribution advantage, similar to Google's past search monopoly case. However, legal processes are slow, and Google doesn't need permission to make Gemini the default on its own Android platform.

While consumer AI benefits from proximity and default status, enterprise AI adoption is different. Enterprise buyers conduct thorough evaluations, which pre-installation alone cannot overcome. Google is addressing this by pushing Gemini through Workspace, but conversion is less straightforward in this market.

headline_marked: [[DDR5 scalper bots now outnumber shoppers 10 to 1]] as 32GB kits surge from $72 to $392
headline: DDR5 scalper bots now outnumber shoppers 10 to 1 as 32GB kits surge from $72 to $392
summary: Automated bots account for 91% of traffic on DDR5 product pages, polling listings every 6.5 seconds. This has driven 32GB DDR5 kits from $72 to $392 in a year, making purchases difficult for consumers.
details: DDR5 memory product pages are being overwhelmed by scalper bots, accounting for 91% of traffic at one retailer, a 10:1 ratio against legitimate shoppers. This bot activity has contributed to a dramatic price increase, with 32GB DDR5-6000 kits surging from an average of $72 to $392 in the last year.

Research by DataDome, a bot-mitigation firm, indicates that listings are polled approximately every 6.5 seconds by automated requests. These bots use cache-busting parameters to bypass cached stock data, targeting both industrial module makers and consumer brands.

The problem is compounded by broader DRAM supply issues. Hyperscale buyers have reportedly placed deposits against most of 2027's DRAM output, and conventional DRAM contract prices are expected to rise another 13-18% in Q3, following a 60% increase in Q2.

Retailers are implementing countermeasures; Framework stopped selling standalone RAM, and Micro Center limits CPU/motherboard/DDR5 bundles to in-store, one-per-household. Newegg and Amazon have also bundled CPUs with memory to deter resellers.

It's important to note that the 91% figure comes from a single unnamed retailer, and DataDome, which sells bot-blocking products, has not published its full methodology. Page requests do not equate to actual purchases, so the precise amount of stock secured by bots remains unquantified.
